chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Abdillah ibn Sinan ibn Sinan, and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Abdillahan ibn Al-Mughirah, and Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, all together from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding accidental killing that is similar to intentional killing, when one kills with a whip or a stick or a stone, the blood money for that is aggravated, and it is one hundred camels: forty of them are Khalifah (camels in their fifth year) between Thaniyyah (fourth year) and Bazl (sixth year) in their year, and thirty are Hiqqah (three-year-old female camel), and thirty are Bint Labun (two-year-old female camel). And for simple error, there are thirty Hiqqah, and thirty Bint Labun, and twenty Bint Makhad (one-year-old female camel), and twenty Ibn Labun (male one-year-old camel). And the value of each camel from silver is one hundred and twenty dirhams, or ten dinars. And from sheep, the value of each Nab (young camel) from camels is twenty sheep.

key_terms.النَّابِ: Young camel (specifically used for valuation equivalence)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific blood money compensation for accidental killing using a tool like a whip or stick according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between simple accidental homicide and 'semi-intentional' killing (khit' shibh al-amd), where the use of a tool like a whip or stone elevates the compensation to one hundred camels. It provides precise details on the age and type of camels required, reflecting the practical application of Shia fiqh in calculating financial restitution (diyah) based on the severity of the act.
